items.q: I learned that, I didn't witness this now. ... But because I'm no witness to that. I'm no witness to that. But I heard that was the way he was killed.

ctx.x: Humanity. Well tell me where Buddy Bolden played. We'll talk about that later. Yeah. Maybe you don't want to talk about it when the machine's on.
All right. Who, who, who, who, who, Buddy Bolden?
Yeah, tell me about Buddy Bolden.

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: Fife-like. Little Fife. Started out around here playing on them. And he was a little tramp around the Orleans for years.

ctx.x: This kind that you play in front of?

Yeah, yeah, yeah. Fife-like. Little Fife. Started out around here playing on them. And he was a little tramp around the Orleans for years. For years and years. And finally, and he's quite a talk of the town after he got famous. And he was, he made himself one of the top clown players in the country, didn't he?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you ever work with Buddy or Yanks or any of those guys? [INTERVIEWEE] No.

ctx.x: I used to play Frankie Deucon there once in a while. He played slide and trombone with Frankie Deucon. Tall, slender, dog, fall, black, cut of hair. He lived across the river. Frankie Deucon. Buddy Johnson lived across the river too. Because you know of him, trombone player. Buddy Johnson. He lived across the river. A little short for him.
Did you ever work with Buddy or Yanks or any of those guys?
No. I used to work with another, with Bunk Johnson. You heard talk of Bunk?
